points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 薛定谔出生于维也纳一个制造油布和防水布的工厂主家庭。他在维也纳的学术高中接受教育，展现出对数学和物理的浓厚兴趣。1906年进入维也纳大学，师从物理学家弗朗茨·埃克斯纳和数学教授威廉·韦尔廷。这一时期他深入研究了热力学和统计力学，为后来的量子力学研究奠定了基础。维也纳的学术环境培养了他严谨的科学思维和对哲学问题的兴趣，这些特质贯穿了他整个学术生涯。
points.descriptionEn: Schrödinger was born in Vienna to a family of manufacturers of oilcloth and waterproof fabrics. He received his education at the Academic Gymnasium in Vienna and developed a strong interest in mathematics and physics. In 1906, he entered the University of Vienna, where he studied under physicist Franz Exner and mathematician Wilhelm Wirtinger. During this period, he delved into thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, laying the foundation for his later work in quantum mechanics. Vienna's academic environment nurtured his rigorous scientific thinking and interest in philosophical questions, which characterized his entire academic career.

points.title: 军旅与助教生涯
points.description: 1911年，薛定谔成为维也纳大学的实验物理学助手，开始专注于研究气体理论。第一次世界大战期间，他作为军官在意大利前线服役，期间继续进行科学研究。战后，他先后在耶拿、斯图加特、布雷斯劳和苏黎世等大学担任教授。这一时期他发表了关于统计力学和热力学的重要论文，特别是在爱因斯坦的固体比热理论方面做出了贡献。维也纳的学术经历塑造了他对物理学的独特见解，使他能够在量子力学革命中发挥关键作用。
points.descriptionEn: In 1911, Schrödinger became an assistant in experimental physics at the University of Vienna, beginning his focus on gas theory. During World War I, he served as an officer on the Italian front while continuing his scientific research. After the war, he held professorships at various universities including Jena, Stuttgart, Breslau, and Zurich. During this period, he published important papers on statistical mechanics and thermodynamics, particularly contributing to Einstein's theory of the specific heat of solids. His Vienna academic experience shaped his unique perspective on physics, enabling him to play a crucial role in the quantum mechanics revolution.

points.title: 量子力学奠基
points.description: 1921年，薛定谔担任苏黎世大学理论物理学教授。正是在苏黎世期间，他完成了物理学史上最重要的工作之一。1926年，他发表了题为《作为本值问题的量子化》的系列论文，提出了著名的薛定谔方程，这是描述量子系统行为的偏微分方程。这一方程成为量子力学的数学基础，使波函数概念得以形式化。他还提出了薛定谔猫思想实验，用以说明量子叠加态的悖论。苏黎世时期是薛定谔学术生涯的巅峰，他的工作彻底改变了人们对微观世界的理解。
points.descriptionEn: In 1921, Schrödinger became a professor of theoretical physics at the University of Zurich. It was during his time in Zurich that he accomplished one of the most important works in physics history. In 1926, he published a series of papers titled 'Quantization as an Eigenvalue Problem,' introducing the famous Schrödinger equation—a partial differential equation describing the behavior of quantum systems. This equation became the mathematical foundation of quantum mechanics, formalizing the concept of wave functions. He also proposed the Schrödinger's cat thought experiment to illustrate the paradoxes of quantum superposition. Zurich represented the peak of Schrödinger's academic career, as his work fundamentally changed humanity's understanding of the microscopic world.

points.title: 柏林巅峰
points.description: 1927年，薛定谔接替普朗克成为柏林大学理论物理学教授，同时成为普鲁士科学院院士。在柏林期间，他与爱因斯坦建立了深厚的友谊，两人经常就量子力学的哲学含义展开讨论。薛定谔对哥本哈根诠释持批评态度，试图发展更符合经典物理学直觉的波动力学。1933年，纳粹上台后，薛定谔作为反对者无法继续留在德国。尽管他在柏林的时间不长，但这一时期他的学术声望达到顶峰，并因创立波动力学而获得诺贝尔物理学奖。柏林的经历使他更加坚定了对科学独立性和学术自由的信念。
points.descriptionEn: In 1927, Schrödinger succeeded Planck as professor of theoretical physics at the University of Berlin and became a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences. During his time in Berlin, he developed a deep friendship with Einstein, with whom he frequently discussed the philosophical implications of quantum mechanics. Schrödinger was critical of the Copenhagen interpretation and attempted to develop wave mechanics that was more consistent with classical physics intuition. In 1933, after the Nazi rise to power, Schrödinger, as an opponent, could no longer remain in Germany. Although his time in Berlin was brief, his academic prestige reached its peak during this period, and he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his development of wave mechanics. His Berlin experience strengthened his commitment to scientific independence and academic freedom.

points.title: 短暂回归
points.description: 1936年，薛定谔回到奥地利，担任格拉茨大学物理学教授。然而，1938年德国吞并奥地利后，薛定谔因其反纳粹立场被立即解雇。这一事件促使他迅速离开奥地利，前往意大利，随后都柏林。格拉茨的短暂经历再次证明了他对政治压迫的抵抗，以及他坚持学术独立性的原则。尽管面临政治压力，薛定谔仍然继续他的研究工作，特别是在生物物理学领域的探索，这为他后来在都柏林的工作奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1936, Schrödinger returned to Austria and became a professor of physics at the University of Graz. However, in 1938, following the German annexation of Austria, Schrödinger was immediately dismissed due to his anti-Nazi stance. This event prompted him to quickly leave Austria for Italy, and subsequently Dublin. His brief experience in Graz once again demonstrated his resistance to political oppression and his commitment to academic independence. Despite the political pressure, Schrödinger continued his research work, particularly in the field of biophysics, which laid the foundation for his later work in Dublin.

points.title: 爱尔兰岁月
points.description: 1940年，薛定谔接受爱尔兰首相德瓦莱拉邀请，担任都柏林高等研究院理论物理学研究所主任。在都柏林的17年里，他继续发展波动力学理论，并拓展到生物物理学领域，出版了《生命是什么》一书，探索量子生物学和遗传密码的早期概念。他还致力于统一场论的研究，试图将引力、电磁力和核力统一起来。1956年，薛定谔返回维也纳，但保留都柏林的职位直到去世。都柏林时期是薛定谔学术生涯的第二个重要阶段，他的跨学科研究对后来的分子生物学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1940, Schrödinger accepted an invitation from Irish Prime Minister Éamon de Valera to become the Director of the School of Theoretical Physics at the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. During his 17 years in Dublin, he continued to develop wave mechanics and expanded into biophysics, publishing the book 'What Is Life?' which explored early concepts of quantum biology and the genetic code. He also worked on unified field theory, attempting to unify gravity, electromagnetism, and nuclear forces. In 1956, Schrödinger returned to Vienna but retained his Dublin position until his death. The Dublin period represented the second major phase of Schrödinger's academic career, and his interdisciplinary research had a profound impact on later molecular biology.

appraisal.zh: 薛定谔通常被视为20世纪最重要的物理学家之一，其波动力学为量子力学奠定了数学基础，薛定谔方程更成为现代物理学的标志性成就；《生命是什么》启发分子生物学的发展，影响克里克、沃森等后来者，薛定谔猫则成为量子悖论的流行象征。不过也有研究者指出，波动力学在解释测量问题与量子纠缠时存在局限，他对哥本哈根诠释的批评未能给出完整替代方案，晚年统一场论尝试亦无突破，其婚外情等个人生活争议在一定程度上影响了公众形象。
appraisal.en: Schrödinger is generally regarded as one of the most important physicists of the twentieth century: his wave mechanics gave quantum mechanics its mathematical foundation, the Schrödinger equation became an iconic achievement of modern physics, and What Is Life? helped inspire molecular biology and later figures such as Crick and Watson, while Schrödinger's cat became a popular symbol of quantum paradox. Yet researchers also note that wave mechanics has limits in explaining measurement and entanglement, that his critique of the Copenhagen interpretation offered no complete alternative, that his later unified field theory attempts brought no breakthrough, and that controversies in his personal life somewhat affected his public image.

supporter.zh: 薛定谔是20世纪最伟大的物理学家之一，他的波动力学理论为量子力学奠定了数学基础，彻底改变了人类对微观世界的理解。他不仅是一位杰出的科学家，还是一位深刻的思想家，其跨学科研究将物理学与生物学、哲学联系起来。薛定谔的学术遗产超越了纯物理学领域，他对生命本质的探索启发了分子生物学的发展。他的科学精神和独立思考的态度激励着一代又一代的科学家追求真理。
supporter.en: Schrödinger is regarded as one of the greatest physicists of the 20th century, whose wave mechanics theory established the mathematical foundation for quantum mechanics and fundamentally changed humanity's understanding of the microscopic world. He was not only an outstanding scientist but also a profound thinker who connected physics with biology and philosophy through interdisciplinary research. Schrödinger's legacy extends beyond pure physics, as his exploration of the nature of life inspired the development of molecular biology. His scientific spirit and independent thinking continue to inspire generations of scientists in their pursuit of truth.

critic.zh: 薛定谔的波力学虽然数学上优美，但在解释测量问题和量子纠缠等量子现象时存在局限性。他对哥本哈根诠释的批评未能提供完整的替代方案，显示出他在量子力学哲学理解上的矛盾。此外，薛定谔在统一场论方面的尝试未能取得突破性进展，反映了他晚年研究方向的局限性。他的个人生活也受到争议，包括婚外情和复杂的人际关系，这些因素在一定程度上影响了他的公众形象和学术声誉。
critic.en: While mathematically elegant, Schrödinger's wave mechanics has limitations in explaining quantum phenomena such as measurement problems and quantum entanglement. His criticism of the Copenhagen interpretation failed to provide a complete alternative, revealing contradictions in his philosophical understanding of quantum mechanics. Additionally, his attempts at unified field theory did not achieve breakthrough results, reflecting limitations in his later research direction. His personal life was also marked by controversy, including extramarital affairs and complex relationships, which somewhat affected his public image and academic reputation.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，薛定谔被定义为量子力学革命的奠基人之一，其薛定谔方程成为现代物理学的标志性成就。他的思想实验，特别是薛定谔猫，已成为量子力学悖论的流行象征，出现在各种科普作品和流行文化中。薛定谔的形象超越了纯粹的科学家，成为科学与哲学交叉的象征人物。他的《生命是什么》一书被视为分子生物学的奠基之作，影响了克里克、沃森等后来的诺贝尔奖得主。薛定谔的跨学科思维和对生命本质的探索使他成为20世纪最具影响力的科学家之一。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture, Schrödinger is recognized as one of the founders of the quantum mechanics revolution, with his equation becoming an iconic achievement of modern physics. His thought experiments, particularly Schrödinger's cat, have become popular symbols of quantum paradoxes, appearing in various scientific works and popular culture. Schrödinger's image transcends that of a mere scientist, representing a figure at the intersection of science and philosophy. His book 'What Is Life?' is considered a foundational work in molecular biology, influencing later Nobel laureates like Crick and Watson. Schrödinger's interdisciplinary thinking and exploration of the nature of life make him one of the most influential scientists of the 20th century.

self.zh: 意识是宇宙的唯一真实存在，物质只是意识的显现。
self.en: Consciousness is the only real thing in the universe, matter is merely a manifestation of consciousness.
